releaseNote.summary: Automatic transitions accept an optional priority: lower is evaluated first, omitted is 100, equal keeps declaration order, the default auto transition stays last.

autoTransitionPriority.description: An automatic transition may declare an optional integer priority (minimum 1). The Auto step evaluates a state's automatic transitions in ascending priority order and the first satisfied rule wins; a transition without priority counts as 100, transitions with equal priority keep their declaration order (stable sort), and the DefaultAutoTransition is always evaluated last. Evaluation is sequential, so cheap and likely rules belong at a low priority number. If a rule's script throws, the step fails and lower-priority rules are not evaluated. The publish validator rejects a priority below 1 and a priority on a manual, shared or start transition or on the DefaultAutoTransition; it warns when automatic transitions of a state share an effective priority, only when at least one of them has an explicit priority. A runtime older than this release ignores priority and evaluates in array order, except that a transition with an absent triggerKind was evaluated before one with an explicit triggerKind 0 and the default (triggerKind 10) came last, so a flow that depends on priority must not be rolled back below it. Requires the runtime version that ships this entry and a vnext-schema release containing transition.priority.
